summary: Tested Stories backend (24 pytest cases) + smoke-tested frontend (StoriesBar, Hidden Viewers, profile entry). 19/24 backend tests pass. CRITICAL BUG: circle-based visibility is completely broken for stories — the stories code queries `db.users.circle` (an array field that is never populated) instead of the actual `db.friendships` collection where circle relationships live. Effect: NOBODY sees anyone else's stories in the feed, view/reply on a circle-member's story returns 403, and hidden_viewers list is always empty. Story creation, own-feed, delete, moderation, quota, anon-restriction, own-story-reply-guard all work correctly. Frontend components render properly (StoriesBar has correct testIDs, HiddenViewers screen loads via `stories-privacy-open`), UI just surfaces the empty backend results.

critical.issue: Circle-membership check reads `db.users.circle` array (never populated). Actual circle relationships live in `db.friendships` collection (see `circle_add` at server.py:5687 which inserts into friendships and never touches users.circle). Result: circle_ids is always empty → every visibility check fails. Verified in Mongo: user_6e65e19525d5 (A) has 1 friendship with user_16f709708760 (B) but users doc has no `circle` field. server.py:5853, 5856-5857, 5997-5998, 6114-6115 all rely on the non-existent field.

minor.issue: Comment >200 chars returns 422 (Pydantic default). Frontend enforces 200 via `maxLength` prop but backend should probably return a friendlier 400 with an Italian message consistent with other body-validation errors.

integration_issues.flow: StoriesBar / HiddenViewers renders empty for authed user with active friendships
integration_issues.issue: This is downstream of the backend circle bug. HiddenViewers screen shows '0 persone · 0 nascoste — Nessuno ti segue' for user A even though user B has A in their circle. Once the backend fix lands, retest UI end-to-end.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): Replace `users.circle` lookups in stories code with reads from the `friendships` collection (source of truth). Concretely, in server.py: (a) line ~5997 `stories_feed` — derive `circle_ids` from `db.friendships.find({'user_id': me},{'friend_id':1})`; (b) `_story_is_visible_to` (5853-5857) — check `db.friendships.count_documents({'user_id':viewer_id,'friend_id':author_id})` instead of `viewer.circle`; (c) `stories_hidden_viewers` (6114-6115) — followers are `db.friendships.find({'friend_id':me},{'user_id':1})` (i.e. anyone who has ME as a friend), then look up user docs. Verify with the existing pytest suite `backend/tests/test_stories.py` — the 5 failing tests should all pass afterwards.
Optional: return 400 (with Italian detail) instead of Pydantic 422 for comment length overflow on POST /api/stories, for consistency with other endpoints.
After backend fix, re-run the frontend smoke test to confirm StoriesBar shows circle members' stories and HiddenViewers lists followers.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:5997 (`stories_feed`) and 5853 (`_story_is_visible_to`) and 6114 (`stories_hidden_viewers`) all read `users.circle` — this field is never written anywhere in server.py (`circle_add` at 5687 only touches `friendships`). This is the root cause of the failing tests and effectively disables the whole stories feature for non-self viewing.

server.py:6152 `reply_to_story`: Nice — reuses existing DM moderation + block-check pipeline via `_send_dm_internal`. Owner-reply guard (400 for self) works.

All 5 currently-failing tests should turn green: test_feed_shows_circle_member_stories, test_stories_by_user_circle_member, test_mark_viewed_idempotent, test_get_hidden_viewers_lists_followers, test_reply_creates_dm. rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: two disjoint data models. The circle feature (added earlier) stores friendships as documents in `db.friendships` with shape `{user_id, friend_id}`. The new stories feature was written assuming an array field `circle` on the user doc. These two models were never bridged — neither `circle_add` writes to `users.circle`, nor does the stories code read from `friendships`. REPRODUCTION: 1) login as chat_a and chat_b (both have `email_verified=true`); 2) POST /api/circle/{userB_id} as A and vice-versa (returns 200); 3) POST /api/stories as A and as B (both return 200); 4) GET /api/stories/feed as A — response `groups` only contains A's own group, missing B. Direct Mongo query confirms `users` doc for A has no `circle` field despite the friendship document existing. MITIGATION: change all four locations in server.py that read `users.circle` / query `{'circle': me}` to instead query `db.friendships`.
